about.title: Poway Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Defective products cause harm everywhere, and Poway households are no exception — whether it's a malfunctioning tool used on a Pomerado Road home project, a faulty vehicle part involved in a crash along Rt 67, or a household appliance that fails without warning. California law gives injured people an important advantage here: strict liability. Under this legal doctrine, you generally don't need to prove a manufacturer was negligent, only that the product was defective in its design, manufacturing, or warnings, and that the defect caused your injury. That said, these cases can involve multiple companies in the supply chain — makers, distributors, retailers — and often require preserving the product itself as evidence. Our team handles product liability claims in San Diego County and can evaluate what happened and explain your options. We work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost.

whyChoose.title: Why Strict Liability Matters for Poway Residents

items.title: No Need to Prove Negligence
items.desc: California's strict liability rule means you typically only need to show the product was defective and caused harm, not that the company was careless in making it.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Be Responsible
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially share liability, which may open more than one path to recovery for your injury.

items.title: Preserving Evidence Matters Early
items.desc: Because the defective product itself is often central evidence, keeping it unaltered and available can meaningfully affect how a claim is evaluated.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer knew about the defect?
items.answer: No. Under California's strict liability approach, you generally don't need to prove the company knew about or intended the defect. You typically just need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was at the time of the incident, including packaging, instructions, and any parts that broke or malfunctioned. Don't attempt repairs or discard anything, since the product itself often serves as key evidence in these claims.

items.question: Does it matter that this happened in Poway specifically?
items.answer: Public crash and injury data show activity along corridors like Poway Road, Pomerado Road, and Rt 67, so vehicle-related product defects are one pattern we're familiar with. We can look at where and how your injury happened and explain how San Diego County courts typically handle these cases.

items.question: Will I have to pay anything upfront?
items.answer: No. We work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
